chapter.name: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

questions.q: In the jar activity four anonymous slips were read out. P: "I have grown taller." Q: "My chest has become wider." R: "New reddish spots have appeared on my face." S: "My breasts have started developing." The teacher asks which two slips could have come from a boy and from a girl alike. Which pair is right?
questions.a: P and R. Height gain and pimples are seen in both boys and girls; a wider chest is noted for boys and development of breasts for girls.
o: P and R
P and Q
Q and S
R and S

questions.q: Nisha is 13 and her brother Om is 9. Using only the typical age range the chapter gives for adolescence, which statement is correct?
questions.a: Nisha is inside the range with up to about 6 years left; Om is about 1 year short of its start. The typical range is 10 to 19 years: 19 - 13 = 6 years remain for Nisha, and 10 - 9 = 1 year for Om.
o: Nisha is inside the range with up to about 6 years left; Om is about 1 year short of its start
Nisha is inside the range with up to about 9 years left; Om is about 1 year short of its start
Nisha is inside the range with up to about 6 years left; Om is already inside it
Nisha has already passed the range; Om is about 1 year short of its start

questions.q: Maya's growth card shows 50 cm at birth, 105 cm at age 5 and 138 cm at age 10. She says, "My body began growing taller only when I became a teenager." Which reply agrees with the chapter?
questions.a: Height has grown since birth; adolescence only makes it more prominent. The chapter says growth, including height, is continuous from birth and becomes more prominent during adolescence.
o: Height has grown since birth; adolescence only makes it more prominent
Height starts increasing only at 10, which is why that age begins adolescence
Height stops increasing after birth and returns only in adolescence
Height rises in adolescence, while weight and strength do not change

questions.q: Varun, 12, sees that three friends' voices have turned hoarse while his has not. His mother wonders whether something is wrong. Which statement could his cousin make using this chapter?
questions.a: Changes come at different times, so a later start can be normal. Timing, nature and extent of the changes vary among individuals, and the variation is completely normal.
o: Changes come at different times, so a later start can be normal
Every boy has a hoarse voice by 12, so Varun should be checked
Voice change is the only sign of adolescence, so Varun has not entered it
Adolescence begins at exactly 10 for all, so Varun's voice is delayed

questions.q: A school nurse's record shows that Mohan gained about 5 cm in a year in Class 5 but about 9 cm in a year in Class 7, and his voice turned hoarse in Class 7. What does this pattern suggest?
questions.a: Adolescence has begun, with rapid growth and a growing voice box. Until about 10-12 years most changes are in height and weight; rapid growth with voice change marks adolescence.
o: Adolescence has begun, with rapid growth and a growing voice box
He has become an adult, so his growth will stop now
Rapid growth happens only in infancy, so the record is wrong
Oily secretions have increased, which alone explains his height gain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about hair growth.
Statement 1: If a boy's hair growth appears later than his friends', it signals a health problem.
Statement 2: A boy who has no chest hair by the age of 16 has not entered adolescence.
Statement 3: Facial hair that later grows into a moustache and a beard is a change many boys develop as they move towards adulthood.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 3 only. Statements 1 and 2 are false: variation in timing of hair growth is completely normal, and chest hair is seen in only some boys, so its absence says nothing about adolescence. Statement 3 is stated in the chapter.
o: 3 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a school survey the share of students with pimples rose from 3% in Class 5 to 25% in Class 7 and 40% in Class 9, which fits the onset of adolescence.
Reason (R): Pimples are caused by the growth of the voice box.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Assertion is true but Reason is false. The assertion is true: acne is a common occurrence in the adolescent years. The reason is false: pimples come from increased oily secretions clogging skin pores, and the voice box causes the hoarse voice.
o: Assertion is true but Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Two boys of the same age may both have a hoarse voice, yet only one shows a visible bump in the throat.
Reason (R): The bump caused by the growth of the voice box is not noticeable in every individual.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion. Voice box growth makes the voice hoarse, but the bump (Adam's apple) is not visible in everyone, which explains the difference.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Match each item in Column I with the matching item in Column II.
Column I: 1. Neha, 14, notices only a slight change in her voice; 2. Ayaan's cousin of his age has a visible bump in the throat but Ayaan has none; 3. Tanvi, 13, has red spots on her cheeks and her friend does not; 4. Dev, 11, has grown 8 cm in a year with no other change yet
Column II: a. Oily secretions clog skin pores; b. The voice box grows less in girls; c. The bump is not noticeable in every individual; d. Until about 10-12 years most changes are in height and weight
questions.a: 1-b, 2-c, 3-a, 4-d. Each situation is explained by the matching idea.

questions.q: (a) Shalu says, "Adolescence brings only physical changes like growing taller or developing body hair." Name two other kinds of change the chapter says come with growing up. (b) Which kind of change can go unnoticed by others, and why?
questions.a: (a) Emotional and behavioural changes, and the ability to reproduce. (b) Internal changes, such as the maturing of the parts involved in reproduction, because they cannot be seen from the outside.
s: Part (a): emotional and behavioural changes (and the ability to reproduce)
Part (b): internal changes go unnoticed since they are not visible

questions.q: Meher, 13, has hair in her armpits. Her cousin Kabir, 15, has a light moustache but no chest or back hair. (a) Is anything in Kabir's hair growth unusual according to the chapter? (b) Which hair growth do Meher and Kabir share?
questions.a: (a) No. Facial hair is common in boys, some boys also get chest and back hair, and a few have no significant hair growth; variation in timing and appearance is normal. (b) Hair in the armpits (and the pubic region).
s: Part (a): not unusual; chest and back hair appear in only some boys
Part (b): armpit and pubic hair is common to boys and girls

questions.q: (a) Arrange in order: pores get clogged, oily secretions from the skin increase, small reddish pimples appear, infection sets in. (b) In which stage of life does this chain become common, and which word names the condition?
questions.a: (a) Oily secretions increase, pores get clogged, infection sets in, pimples appear. (b) Adolescence; the condition is acne.
s: Part (a): correct order of the chain
Part (b): adolescence and acne

questions.q: A farmer says, "My one-month-old calf eats well and grows fast, so it will soon have a calf of its own." (a) Give the chapter's idea that shows the farmer is wrong. (b) Name the human stage in which the body prepares for the same ability.
questions.a: (a) Animals need to grow and reach maturity before they can reproduce, so quick growth does not make the calf capable yet. (b) Adolescence.
s: Part (a): growth must reach maturity first
Part (b): adolescence prepares the body for adulthood and reproduction

questions.q: True or False: Armpit hair and hair in the pubic region appear only in boys, so a 12-year-old girl who has armpit hair has an unusual change.
questions.a: False. Both boys and girls grow hair in the armpits and the pubic region; facial hair is the hair that boys often develop, and variation in its timing is completely normal.
s: Verdict: false
Both sexes grow armpit and pubic hair; only facial hair is typical of boys

questions.q: Describe a classroom situation in which two healthy students of the same age look very different in height or voice. Explain what it tells you about adolescence.
questions.a: Any realistic situation, e.g. one boy has a hoarse voice and another does not. It shows timing and extent of change vary and that this is normal.
s: Realistic situation with two students
Timing and extent vary
Variation is normal

questions.q: Seema writes in her notebook: "Boys get an Adam's apple and a hoarse voice; in girls the voice never changes at all." Is she fully right, partly right or wrong? Check her claim.
questions.a: Partly right. The boys' part is right, as the voice box grows. But girls' voice box also grows, though less, so there is a slight change in voice. 'Never' makes the second half wrong.
s: Boys' part is right: voice box growth, hoarse voice
Girls: voice box grows less, slight change
Verdict: partly right, the absolute second half is false

questions.q: Ramesh, 11, has a few pimples on his face. His friend Kunal, also 11, has none. Ramesh's mother says it is because of the biological changes of growing up. Explain (i) why her remark is possible at 11, and (ii) why Kunal's clear skin need cause no worry.
questions.a: (i) Adolescence typically begins around 10 years, and in it oily secretions of the skin increase, clog the pores and can lead to infection, giving pimples (acne). (ii) The timing and extent of such changes vary among individuals and the variation is normal.
s: Age near the start of adolescence
Cause: more oily secretions clog pores
Timing varies, so Kunal is normal

questions.q: A school ran the jar activity in two classes of 60 students each. Class 5 (ages about 10-11): 48 slips named height and weight, 6 named voice, hair or skin changes, and 6 named other things. Class 8 (ages about 13-14): 21 named height and weight, 27 named voice, hair or skin changes, and 12 named other things. (a) Work out each class's percentage for height and weight and for voice, hair or skin changes. (b) Describe the shift between the classes. (c) Link it to the chapter's statement about 10-12 years. (d) Why can the survey not show that every Class 8 student has entered adolescence?
questions.a: (a) Class 5: 48/60 = 80% height and weight, 6/60 = 10% voice, hair or skin. Class 8: 21/60 = 35% and 27/60 = 45%. (b) Height and weight fall from 80% to 35% while voice, hair and skin changes rise from 10% to 45%. (c) The chapter says that until around 10-12 years most changes are in height and weight, after which other noticeable changes begin and mark adolescence. (d) Slips are anonymous counts of changes, not a record per student, and the timing of changes varies among individuals.
s: Part (b): shift from height and weight to other changes
Part (c): ties the shift to the 10-12 years statement and the onset of adolescence
Part (d): anonymous counts do not give each student's stage
Part (d): timing varies among individuals

questions.q:
A teacher in Pune collected 40 anonymous slips from Class 7 students aged 12-13 listing changes they had noticed: 18 slips named height and weight, 9 named a cracking or hoarse voice, 8 named small reddish spots on the face, and 5 named new hair growth.
(a) What percentage of the slips were about height and weight, and which stage of life do such changes mark?
(b) The voice slips came only from boys. Name the structure behind them and explain why the girls wrote none.
(c) Boys and girls both wrote about the spots. Explain their cause.
(d) The teacher has time for one talk. Spots and voice together account for 17 of 40 slips (42.5%), height for 18 (45%). Which topic would you choose and why?
questions.a: (a) 45%; adolescence. (b) Voice box; it also grows in girls but less, giving only a slight change. (c) Increased oily secretions clog pores (acne). (d) Either, if justified: e.g. height is the commonest, but spots and voice show variations that worry students; a talk stressing that timing varies and is normal covers both.
s: Part (a): 45% and adolescence
Part (b): voice box; slight change in girls
Part (c): oily secretions clog pores
Part (d): justified choice using the data

questions.q: A magazine says: "If at 15 you have no pimples, no hoarse voice and no moustache, you have not entered adolescence." Evaluate this statement using the chapter. Give four separate reasons and a verdict.
questions.a: The statement is not correct. (1) Pimples, voice change and moustache are only some of the visible changes; others are rapid height gain, broader shoulders or breasts, and hair in armpits and the pubic region. (2) Pimples and the Adam's apple are not seen in every individual, and a few boys have no significant hair growth. (3) Moustache is a boys' change and girls' voice changes only slightly, so the three signs cannot apply to everyone. (4) Timing, nature and extent of the changes vary and some changes are internal and unseen. Verdict: the absence of these three signs does not prove adolescence has not begun.
s: Other visible changes exist (height, body structure, hair in armpits)
Some changes are not seen in every individual
Signs are specific to one sex, so they cannot apply to all
Variation in timing and internal changes
Verdict: statement is not correct

questions.q:
At a health camp in a Nashik school the heights of two Class 8 students, Aarav and Bina, were recorded each year from age 10 to 13. Aarav: 140, 145, 151 and 160 cm. Bina: 138, 144, 150 and 154 cm. At 13 Aarav has a hoarse voice and a thin moustache line, while Bina has hair in her armpits and a few pimples. Aarav's father says, "Aarav grew 9 cm this year and Bina only 4 cm, so Aarav is in adolescence and Bina is not."
(a) What was Aarav's largest yearly gain, and how much more height did he gain than Bina over the three years?
(b) Which of the four changes noted at 13 are seen in both boys and girls?
(c) Give the cause of Bina's pimples.
(d) Evaluate the father's claim using the data and the chapter.
questions.a: (a) 9 cm (151 to 160 cm); Aarav gained 20 cm and Bina 16 cm, so 4 cm more. (b) Hair in the armpits and pimples. (c) Increased oily secretions clog the skin pores and can lead to infection. (d) The claim is not supported: Bina's armpit hair and pimples are changes of adolescence, so she is in it too; a smaller height gain in one year shows the pace differs, which is normal, and height is not the only sign.
s: Part (a): 9 cm and 4 cm more
Part (b): armpit hair and pimples
Part (c): oily secretions clog pores
Part (d): Bina is in adolescence by other signs; pace varies

questions.q: Radhika's first period came at 12. If her menstruation stops naturally at 45, the youngest age the chapter gives, she will have menstruated for ___ years.
The Class 7 science club lists four changes seen in adolescents and asks which one is NOT a secondary sexual characteristic. Which one is it?
questions.a: Start of the menstrual cycle in a girl. The menstrual cycle is directly involved in reproduction, whereas the others only help distinguish males from females.
o: Start of the menstrual cycle in a girl
Hoarse voice in a boy
Growth of facial and chest hair in a boy
Development of breasts in a girl

questions.q: Meena's periods began on 5 January, 2 February and 8 March 2026. A friend says, "Your second gap is too long, since the cycle is always 28 days." Which statement fits the chapter?
questions.a: The gaps are 28 and 34 days; both lie in the healthy 21-35 day range. 5 Jan to 2 Feb is 28 days and 2 Feb to 8 Mar is 34 days; 28-30 days is the general pattern but healthy cycles range from 21 to 35 days.
o: The gaps are 28 and 34 days; both lie in the healthy 21-35 day range
The gaps are 28 and 34 days; the second is unhealthy because it exceeds 30 days
The gaps are 28 and 35 days; both are healthy since 28 is the usual cycle
The gaps are 28 and 34 days; neither can be judged, as only the discharge phase counts

questions.q: Ankit, 15, has a hoarse voice and facial hair; his cousin Neha, 13, has begun developing breasts. Their teacher says both are entering puberty. Which reasoning backs her?
questions.a: They are secondary sexual characteristics that mark puberty's onset. Secondary sexual characteristics are natural signs of preparing for adulthood and mark the onset of puberty, the stage of becoming capable of reproduction.
o: They are secondary sexual characteristics that mark puberty's onset
These are organs directly involved in reproduction, so puberty is complete
These changes appear only after the menstrual cycle has begun
These are internal changes that show the reproductive parts have matured

questions.q: Three girls record these values. Reena: cycle 24 days, discharge 4 days. Sara: cycle 36 days, discharge 5 days. Tina: cycle 29 days, discharge 8 days. Using the ranges in the chapter, which statement is correct?
questions.a: Sara's cycle and Tina's discharge lie outside the ranges. Healthy cycles: 21-35 days; discharge: three to seven days.
o: Sara's cycle and Tina's discharge lie outside the ranges
Only Reena's values lie inside the ranges given in the book
Only Sara's cycle lies outside the ranges given in the book
All three records lie inside the ranges given in the book

questions.q: At a parents' meeting, a speaker makes four statements about menstruation. Which one contradicts the chapter?
questions.a: A girl must be kept apart from others during her period. The chapter calls physical isolation a myth with no scientific basis; the other statements are in the chapter.
o: A girl must be kept apart from others during her period
Some girls feel discomfort in the lower abdomen during menstruation
Healthy cycles in girls may be as short as 21 days in length
The cycle is one of the signs of good reproductive health

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about menstruation.
Statement 1: A girl whose menstruation lasts 7 days in a 35-day cycle is within the ranges the chapter gives.
Statement 2: A girl who feels discomfort in the lower abdomen during menstruation has an abnormal cycle.
Statement 3: Menstruation and the menstrual cycle are two names for exactly the same period of days.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only. Statement 1 is true (3-7 days and 21-35 days). Statement 2 is false: only some girls feel discomfort, and it does not make a cycle abnormal. Statement 3 is false: menstruation is the discharge phase inside the cycle.
o: 1 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Girls should not be isolated during menstruation.
Reason (R): Menstruation lasts three to seven days.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Both true, but the duration does not explain why isolation is wrong; the reason is that it is natural and isolation has no scientific basis.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A girl whose cycle is 35 days long has an unhealthy cycle.
Reason (R): The menstrual cycle generally recurs every 28-30 days.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Assertion is false but Reason is true. The assertion is false: healthy cycles range from 21 to 35 days. The reason is true: 28-30 days is the general pattern, but not the limit of what is healthy.
o: Assertion is false but Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false

questions.q:
Match each item in Column I with the matching item in Column II.
Column I: 1. A girl whose discharge lasts 4 days in a 29-day cycle; 2. Mrs Sethi, 52, whose periods stopped naturally; 3. A family keeping a girl apart from others during her period; 4. A boy's moustache and a girl's breast development
Column II: a. A myth with no scientific basis; b. Secondary sexual characteristics; c. The end of reproductive capability, usual at 45-55; d. Menstruation is a phase inside the longer cycle
questions.a: 1-d, 2-c, 3-a, 4-b. Discharge phase within the cycle; natural end of menstruation; myth of isolation; secondary sexual characteristics.

questions.q:
A school health club kept anonymous records of period start dates in 2026. Girl X: 6 Jan, 3 Feb, 3 Mar. Girl Y: 10 Jan, 14 Feb, 22 Mar. Girl Z: 12 Jan, 2 Feb, 20 Feb. X's discharge lasted 5 days, counting 6 Jan as day one.
(a) Find the two cycle lengths of Y and of Z.
(b) Which of those four cycles lie outside the range the chapter calls healthy?
(c) On what date did X's first discharge end, and for how many days of her 28-day cycle was there no discharge?
(d) A visiting doctor can see only one of the two girls Y and Z this week. Whom would you send, and why?
questions.a: (a) Y: 35 and 36 days; Z: 21 and 18 days. (b) Y's 36 and Z's 18 (healthy range is 21 to 35 days). (c) 10 January; 28 - 5 = 23 days. (d) Either, with a reason from the data: Z, since her second cycle is 3 days below the lowest healthy value while Y's is only 1 above the highest; or Y, since her cycles are both at the top of the range. Either way, the girls are to be treated as normal members of the class and not isolated.
s: Part (b): 36 and 18
Part (c): 10 January and 23 days
Part (d): justified choice using distance from the range

questions.q: Imran, 13, says, "I have no hoarse voice and no moustache yet, so my body is not preparing for adulthood." (a) Name the kind of change that includes voice change and facial hair in boys. (b) Give two reasons why Imran's inference may be wrong.
questions.a: (a) Secondary sexual characteristics. (b) Some changes are internal, such as the maturing of the parts involved in reproduction, and cannot be seen; and the timing of changes varies from person to person.
s: Part (a): secondary sexual characteristics
Part (b): internal changes are unseen and timing varies

questions.q: Zainab's periods began on 3 July and 5 August 2026. (a) Find the length of her cycle. (b) Her friend says only a 28-day cycle is healthy. Use the chapter to reply.
questions.a: (a) 33 days. (b) 28-30 days is the general pattern, but healthy cycles range from 21 to 35 days, so 33 days is healthy.
s: Part (a): 33 days
Part (b): 21-35 days is the healthy range

questions.q: True or False: Latha's period lasted 5 days and her next one began 29 days after the first. So her menstrual cycle is 5 days long.
questions.a: False. The 5 days are only the menstruation (discharge) phase, which may last three to seven days; the menstrual cycle is the whole process that recurs, here 29 days.
s: Verdict: false
Menstruation is the discharge phase; the cycle is the whole 29 days

questions.q: Mrs Rao, 52, has not had a period for a year. Her niece Diya, 12, asks whether she is ill. (a) What does the chapter say about the age at which menstruation stops? (b) What does its stopping mark?
questions.a: (a) It usually stops naturally by the age of 45-55 years, so a stop at 52 is natural. (b) The end of the reproductive capability in a woman's life.
s: Part (a): usually by 45-55 years, so natural
Part (b): end of reproductive capability

questions.q: Give a school situation in which a girl may feel unnecessary fear or shame about menstruation because of a myth, and write the one scientific fact a classmate could say to help her.
questions.a: Any realistic situation, e.g. a girl is told to sit apart during her period and feels ashamed. Fact: menstruation is a natural process and a sign of good reproductive health; isolation has no scientific basis.
s: Realistic situation showing fear or shame from a myth
Scientific fact: natural process, no basis for isolation

questions.q: A school health club recorded five girls' cycles. Aditi: cycle 28 days, discharge 5 days. Bhavna: 21 and 3. Charu: 36 and 6. Deepa: 30 and 9. Esha: 35 and 7. (a) Which records lie inside both ranges given in the chapter, and which lie outside, with the reason? (b) For each girl inside both ranges, find the days of the cycle with no discharge. (c) Which of them follows the general 28-30 day pattern? (d) Why would calling Bhavna or Esha unhealthy, or keeping them apart, be wrong?
questions.a: (a) Inside both ranges (cycle 21-35 days, discharge 3-7 days): Aditi, Bhavna, Esha. Outside: Charu (cycle 36 is above 35) and Deepa (discharge 9 is above 7). (b) Aditi 28 - 5 = 23 days, Bhavna 21 - 3 = 18 days, Esha 35 - 7 = 28 days. (c) Only Aditi (28 days); Bhavna and Esha are healthy but not in the general pattern. (d) Healthy cycles range from 21 to 35 days, and menstruation is natural; isolation is a myth with no scientific basis.
s: Part (a): Aditi, Bhavna, Esha inside; Charu and Deepa outside with reasons
Part (b): 23, 18 and 28 days
Part (c): only Aditi follows 28-30 days
Part (d): healthy range 21-35 days
Part (d): natural process; isolation has no scientific basis

questions.q: Rohit says: "A girl whose period comes after 25 days has a health problem, because the cycle is always 28 days." Evaluate his statement.
questions.a: He is wrong. The cycle generally recurs every 28-30 days but healthy cycles may range from 21 to 35 days, so 25 days can be healthy. 'Always' makes it false.
s: Verdict: incorrect
28-30 days is only the general pattern
21-35 days is the healthy range

questions.q: Write the dates of the start of two successive periods of a girl (use any months of 2026) whose cycle is healthy according to the chapter but is longer than the general 28-30 day pattern. Show the length and say why it is healthy.
questions.a: Any valid pair, e.g. 3 March and 5 April 2026: 3 March to 3 April is 31 days and 5 April is 33 days. The length is above 30 but within the healthy range of 21 to 35 days.
s: A pair of dates with a correct cycle length shown
Length greater than 30 days
Within the healthy range of 21 to 35 days

questions.q: A magazine says: "In a 28-day cycle, Pooja's menstruation lasted 31 days." Show that this cannot be correct.
questions.a: Menstruation is only one phase of the cycle, so it cannot last longer than the cycle. 31 is more than 28. Also, menstruation lasts only three to seven days.
s: Menstruation is a phase of the cycle
31 is greater than 28
Normal duration is three to seven days

questions.q:
Radhika, 12, had her first period last month, with discharge lasting 5 days and a cycle of 30 days. She feels pain in the lower abdomen on the first two days of each period. Her grandmother, 58, says her own periods stopped at 50, and her aunt, 47, still has regular periods. The family considers two plans. Plan P: Radhika rests at home on days 1 and 2 of each period, not separated from anyone, and goes to school from day 3. Plan Q: she attends school every day, with permission to rest in the sick room when needed.
(a) Between what two total numbers of years may Radhika expect to menstruate, using the chapter's end ages?
(b) Are the grandmother's and the aunt's experiences consistent with the chapter?
(c) Under Plan P, what fraction of each 30-day cycle is spent at home, and for how many days is there no discharge?
(d) Choose between P and Q and justify your choice, naming the condition from the chapter that must hold for either plan.
questions.a: (a) 33 to 43 years (45 - 12 and 55 - 12). (b) Yes; periods usually stop by 45-55 years, so 50 and a continuing cycle at 47 are both natural. (c) 2/30 = 1/15 (about 6.7%); 30 - 5 = 25 days without discharge. (d) Either, with a reason: P suits her discomfort on the first days; Q keeps her in class and treats menstruation as natural. The condition for both: she is not isolated or shamed, since isolation is a myth with no scientific basis.
s: Part (a): 33 to 43 years
Part (b): consistent with 45-55 years
Part (c): 1/15 (about 6.7%) and 25 days
Part (d): justified choice and the no-isolation condition

questions.q: A panchayat proposes: "Girls must stay at home for 7 days of every 28-day cycle because of menstruation." Evaluate the proposal. (a) What share of the cycle would be spent at home, compared with the least the chapter's discharge duration allows (3 days)? (b) Judge the proposal using the chapter on duration, nature and myths, and give your verdict.
questions.a: (a) 7/28 = 25% of the cycle against 3/28, about 10.7%; the rule treats the longest duration as fixed for all. (b) Menstruation lasts three to seven days and varies; it is a natural process and a sign of good reproductive health; isolation is a myth that causes unnecessary fear, shame or guilt and has no scientific basis. Verdict: the proposal should be rejected.
s: 25% and about 10.7%
Duration varies, so a fixed 7 days overstates
Natural process, sign of good reproductive health
Isolation is a myth causing fear, shame or guilt, no scientific basis
Verdict: reject with the reasoning

questions.q: Sara writes three diary lines. P: "Even a small remark makes me feel very hurt." Q: "Since the fair I have suddenly started reading about birds every evening." R: "I dance for an hour after school and feel calmer." Which option labels P, Q and R correctly as an emotional change, an effect on behaviour and a way for positive growth?
questions.a: P: emotional change; Q: effect on behaviour; R: way for positive growth. Increased sensitivity is an emotional change, a deeper interest in a new area is an effect on behaviour, and dance is one of the varied activities that help positive growth.
o: P: emotional change; Q: effect on behaviour; R: way for positive growth
P: effect on behaviour; Q: emotional change; R: way for positive growth
P: emotional change; Q: way for positive growth; R: effect on behaviour
P: way for positive growth; Q: effect on behaviour; R: emotional change

questions.q: In a class of 50, each student named one thing. 21 named mood swings, 12 named being deeply hurt by small remarks, 9 named a deeper interest in a new area, and 8 named joining a drive to help the needy. What percentage of the class named an emotional change rather than an effect on behaviour?
questions.a: 66%. Mood swings and increased sensitivity are emotional changes: (21 + 12) / 50 = 66%. Interest and social initiatives are effects on behaviour.

questions.q: Dev, 8, and his cousin Dia, 14, both lose the finals of a school race. Based on the chapter, which expectation is most reasonable?

questions.q: A counsellor asked 48 Class 7 students to name one thing. 18 named mood swings, 12 increased sensitivity, 10 a deeper interest in a new area, and 8 joining a social initiative. questions.q:
Aarti, 13, kept a five-day diary. Monday: delighted in the morning, in tears at a classmate's remark at 1 pm. Tuesday: three hours reading about volcanoes. Part (c): Wednesday and dance as a varied activity

Understanding emotions helps better choices and thoughtful responses

Part (b): emotional changes

questions.q:

Part (d): pads or peer education linked to the chapter

All three needs covered
Each item matched to its need

Iron for blood and the problem a lack causes
Vitamin B12 must come from food

Part (b): incident (iii), sharing without consent

questions.q: The 'Don'ts' column of the chapter's social media table has only one entry printed. Write two more don'ts that follow from the chapter and say which kind of cyberbullying each prevents.
questions.a: Any two valid: do not spread false rumours (false rumours); do not send misleading messages (misleading messages); do not share another person's personal information without consent (sharing personal information); do not upload pictures carelessly.
s: Don't 1 with the kind it prevents
Don't 2 with the kind it prevents

questions.q: True or False: Since regular exercise keeps the body fit and builds stamina, a teenager who plays sports daily can safely skip a balanced diet.
questions.a: False. Exercise keeps body and mind fit, but the chapter says a nutritious diet is of utmost importance in adolescence; exercise does not replace it.
s: Verdict: false
A nutritious diet remains of utmost importance; exercise does not replace it

questions.q: In the Class 7 group chat, Dev spread an untrue story that Anu cheated, Raj forwarded it, Meena posted a screenshot of Anu's private message, Sam sent Kabir a false message that the test was cancelled, and Tina told Anu to speak to the class teacher. (a) Classify the actions of Dev, Raj, Meena and Sam. (b) Which table do or dos did they ignore? (c) What should Anu do, and how does Tina's advice fit the chapter?
questions.a: (a) Dev: false rumour; Raj: spreading the false rumour further; Meena: sharing personal information without consent; Sam: misleading message. (b) Think before posting, be respectful and kind, and protect privacy. (c) Anu should not feel scared or helpless, handle it wisely and seek help from parents and teachers; Tina's advice matches this.
s: Dev and Raj: false rumour
Meena: personal information without consent; Sam: misleading message
Dos ignored: think before posting, respectful and kind, protect privacy
Anu: not scared or helpless, handle wisely
Seek help from parents and teachers, matching Tina's advice

questions.q: Ria, 13, has started copying the way a popular older student speaks and posts. (a) Name the tendency of adolescents this shows. (b) Which of the table's dos would help her most, and why?
questions.a: (a) Mimicking the behaviour of peers. (b) Think before posting, because it makes her check whether the borrowed words or actions are respectful and suit her before they go online.
s: Part (a): mimicking peers
Part (b): think before posting, with a reason

questions.q: An unknown online 'friend' invites Meena to a private video chat and asks her to keep it secret from her parents. (a) Which caution from the chapter applies? (b) Whom should she go to, and what does the chapter say they can help with?
questions.a: (a) Be cautious about sharing personal information with strangers online. (b) Parents or teachers; guidance from elders and teachers helps use platforms positively and safely.
s: Part (a): caution about strangers and personal information
Part (b): parents or teachers, guidance

questions.q:
A Coimbatore school surveyed its 80 Class 7 students. Each chose the one statement that fitted them best: 32 post photos publicly, 20 have been the target of a false rumour in a chat, 12 have been asked for personal information by a stranger, and 16 reported none. The pledge can hold only three of five rules: A think before posting; B protect privacy; C be respectful and kind; D do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends; E seek help from parents or teachers if bullied.
(a) What percentage of students were the target of a false rumour, and what is that behaviour called?
(b) Which rule answers the 12 students who were asked for information by a stranger?
(c) What percentage post photos publicly, and which chapter caution does it raise?
(d) Choose three rules for the pledge and justify them with the data.
questions.a: (a) 20/80 = 25%; cyberbullying. (b) Rule D, do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends (and be cautious with personal information). (c) 32/80 = 40%; the caution about uploading pictures and protecting privacy. (d) Any three justified by data, e.g. B or D (40% post photos publicly, 15% asked by strangers), E (25% faced a rumour) and A (thinking before posting prevents rumours spreading). Rules C and one of B or D are also defensible.
s: Part (a): 25% and cyberbullying
Part (b): rule D
Part (c): 40% and caution about uploading pictures
Part (d): three rules justified using the survey

questions.q: Tara posts an embarrassing photo of a classmate saying: "It is only a joke and it is my own account." Evaluate her reasoning.
questions.a: Incorrect. Sharing personal pictures or information without consent to make fun of someone is cyberbullying, whatever the account. She should think before posting and protect privacy.
s: Verdict: incorrect
Without consent, making fun is cyberbullying
Think before posting / respect privacy

questions.q: Write a three-line chat in which a student politely declines a stranger's request for her photos, names the rule she is following, and says whom she will tell.
questions.a: Any valid chat, e.g. Stranger: send me your photo. Student: Sorry, I do not share my personal photos with strangers. I will tell my teacher about this request.
s: Polite refusal
Names the rule: no personal photos with strangers or virtual friends
Seeks help from parent or teacher

questions.q: Jay spends three hours online daily and does no sport; Ira spends one hour online and plays badminton for 45 minutes. A friend says, "The chapter proves Jay's three hours online are harmful." Compare the two students and say what the chapter does and does not support.
questions.a: Ira gets the benefits the chapter names for exercise: stamina, a fit body and mind, and a better mood. Jay misses those benefits. The chapter asks for responsible use of platforms and guidance from elders but gives no time limit, so it does not prove three hours are harmful.
s: Ira: stamina, fitness, mood benefits
Jay misses exercise benefits
Chapter gives no time limit, so the friend's claim is not supported

questions.q:
Ishaan, 13, joined an online group and began copying the rude comments of an older boy he admires. He also gave his address to a person he had never met. His parents can choose: Plan P: phone only for one hour each evening in the family hall. Plan Q: free phone use but football at school five days a week. Plan R: phone after homework, 30 minutes of football three days a week, and a monthly talk with a teacher.
(a) Which adolescent tendency does his copying show?
(b) Which two actions go against the social media dos and don'ts?
(c) Name two benefits of the football in Plans Q and R.
(d) Pick a plan and defend it, naming one weakness of it.
questions.a: (a) Mimicking peers. (b) Being rude instead of respectful and kind, and sharing personal information with a stranger. (c) Fitness, stamina, mood boost. (d) E.g. Plan R: combines responsible use, exercise and guidance from elders; weakness: less exercise than Q.
s: Part (a): mimicking peers
Part (b): two actions
Part (c): two benefits
Part (d): plan, reason, weakness

questions.q: A school considers replacing the Class 7 sports period with an extra study period, saying, "Sport does not help in studies." Evaluate the proposal using the chapter. Give four separate points and a verdict.
questions.a: The chapter does not support dropping the period. (1) Regular exercise keeps both body and mind fit. (2) It builds stamina. (3) It boosts mood, useful when adolescence brings stronger emotions and mood swings. (4) The chapter asks for a balanced social life: being polite and respectful in person and online, which sport in a team helps practise. Verdict: keep the period, though the chapter says nothing about marks, so no claim about study results can be made from it.
s: Exercise keeps body and mind fit
Builds stamina
Boosts mood during emotional changes of adolescence
Balanced social life and teamwork
Verdict with the limit of the chapter

questions.q: Four teenagers are described. Which one fits the chapter's meaning of substance abuse?
questions.a: Imran, who began smoking beedis months ago and now needs one daily. Substance abuse is regular use that follows the strong urge to take an addictive substance again and again; a single try, a refusal or a prescribed medicine does not fit.
o: Imran, who began smoking beedis months ago and now needs one daily
Joseph, who tried a cigarette once at a wedding and never touched one again
Kavya, who was offered gutka by a classmate but said NO
Lalit, who takes cough syrup prescribed by his doctor for a week

questions.q: Lalit chews gutka daily and cannot manage a day without it. In the chapter's term, this regular use of a harmful substance is called ___.
questions.a: substance abuse

questions.q: A district office wants one programme that fits both the method and the special focus of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. Which plan does so?
questions.a: Youth and women's groups run awareness drives for primary-school children. The Abhiyaan spreads awareness through active participation of the youth, women and community, with a special focus on preventing substance abuse among early-age children.
o: Youth and women's groups run awareness drives for primary-school children
Doctors give a lecture on lung damage only to Class 12 students in the hall
A treatment camp is held only for adults who are already addicted to them
A helpline desk is set up in the office, with no programme in the field

questions.q: Ravi makes four statements about harmful substances. Which one shows that he has misunderstood how they act?
questions.a: "I can try it once and then quit whenever I like". The chapter says these substances are addictive and create a strong urge to take them again and again; the other statements agree with the chapter.
o: "I can try it once and then quit whenever I like"
"Once started, the urge to take it again can grow"
"Smoke from beedis over years can damage the lungs"
"Talking to a trusted person is the first step to stop"

questions.q: Four observations are made about teenagers. P: periods begin in a Class 7 girl. Q: memory loss in a man after years of heavy alcohol use. R: sudden mood swings in a Class 8 boy. S: breathing difficulty in a long-time smoker. Which pair does the chapter attribute to hormones?
questions.a: P and R. Menstruation and other signs of puberty are mainly due to hormones, and some hormones influence mood and behaviour; memory loss and breathing difficulty are listed as effects of harmful substances.
o: P and R
P and Q
Q and S
R and S

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about hormones.
Statement 1: A hormone is released at an appropriate time in response to a signal from the brain.
Statement 2: All hormones influence mood and behaviour.
Statement 3: Menstruation and other signs of puberty are mainly due to hormones.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 is false: the chapter says some hormones influence mood and behaviour, not all. Statements 1 and 3 are stated in the chapter.
o: 1 and 3 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Hormones are produced in different parts of the body.
Reason (R): Hormones are released at an appropriate time in response to signals from the brain.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Both statements are true, but the signals from the brain describe how hormones are released, not why they are produced in different parts of the body.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Some hormones influence mood and behaviour.
Reason (R): All hormones are food nutrients that must be obtained from the diet.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Assertion is true but Reason is false. The assertion is true. The reason is false: hormones are chemicals produced in the body, unlike nutrients and vitamin B12 that come from food.
o: Assertion is true but Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q: A friend says, "It is only one time." Write a three-line reply that says NO as the speech bubble in the chapter advises, names one harm, and names one source of help.
questions.a: Any valid reply, e.g. 'No, I say NO the first time and every time. These substances can cause breathing difficulties and memory loss. I will talk to my teacher if you keep pushing.'
s: Says NO the first time and every time
Names one harm (breathing difficulties, memory loss, lung damage)
Names a source of help (parents, teachers, counselling)

questions.q: Dilip says, "Substances like gutka only harm the lungs, so someone who avoids smoking and chews gutka is safe. Anyway he can stop whenever he wants." Evaluate his claim.
questions.a: Wrong. The chapter lists gutka among harmful substances that are addictive and harm physical and mental health, with effects such as breathing difficulties, memory loss and lung damage depending on the substance. Addiction creates a strong urge to repeat, so stopping is not simply a matter of wanting to.
s: Verdict: wrong
Harm to physical and mental health, not only the lungs
Addictive, strong urge to repeat, not easy to stop

questions.q: Figure 6.5 in the chapter shows a pair of lungs before and after prolonged exposure to beedi or cigarette smoke, with a speech bubble beside it. (a) What does the caption say the pair of pictures shows? (b) What idea about 'just one time' does the speech bubble give?
questions.a: (a) The condition of the lungs before and after prolonged exposure to beedi or cigarette smoke, not after one try. (b) Someone who is addicted today might have started with 'just one time'; say NO the first time and every time.
s: Part (a): after prolonged exposure
Part (b): addiction can start with one try; say NO every time

questions.q: Differentiate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan from the National De-addiction Helpline 14446 by their purpose and by who is involved.
questions.a: The Abhiyaan spreads awareness about avoiding substance abuse through active participation of the youth, women and community, with a special focus on early-age children. The helpline deals with drug addiction and helps drug addicts.
s: Abhiyaan: awareness, youth/women/community, focus on early-age children
Helpline: deals with drug addiction and helps addicts

questions.q: A student says, "Hormones and vitamin B12 are the same kind of thing, since both are needed for a healthy adolescent." Using this chapter and the nutrition section, state one way they differ in origin and what each does.
questions.a: Hormones are chemicals produced in the body and released on signals from the brain, regulating growth and development; vitamin B12 cannot be made in the body and has to be obtained from food, and it is required for proper functioning of the body.
s: Hormones: made in the body, regulate growth and development
B12: cannot be made in the body, comes from food

questions.q: Riya and Rina are both 12. Riya has started her periods; Rina has not. (a) Name the chemicals mainly responsible for such changes. (b) Using what the chapter says about their release, say whether Rina's body must be at fault.
questions.a: (a) Hormones. (b) No. They are released at an appropriate time in response to signals from the brain, and the timing of adolescent changes varies among individuals, so Rina need not be at fault.
s: Part (a): hormones
Part (b): released at an appropriate time; timing varies, so no fault

questions.q: True or False: Menstruation and some mood changes in adolescence can both be traced to hormones, so a girl's physical and emotional changes are linked.
questions.a: True. The chapter says menstruation and other signs of puberty are mainly due to hormones, and some hormones influence mood and behaviour, so one kind of chemical links the physical and emotional changes.
s: Verdict: true
Hormones cause puberty signs and some influence mood

questions.q:
A Bhopal school holds a Nasha Mukt awareness week. Karthik tells his class that his 17-year-old cousin began with a cigarette 'just one time' at a party. Now he gets breathless on stairs, forgets his homework, and has a stomach upset after meals. The school may either (X) run sessions for Class 6-8 with youth volunteers or (Y) hold one assembly for all classes with the helpline displayed.
(a) Which two of the cousin's problems match the chapter's list of effects?
(b) Why can't he stop easily?
(c) Whom should Karthik ask his cousin to approach?
(d) Choose X or Y and justify using the Abhiyaan's focus.
questions.a: (a) Breathing difficulty and memory loss. (b) The substance is addictive and creates a strong urge to repeat. (c) Family, friends, parents or teachers; counselling and medical advice; helpline 14446. (d) X, since the focus is prevention among early-age children; or Y with the reason that it reaches older students and shows the helpline.
s: Part (a): breathing difficulty and memory loss
Part (b): addiction and urge
Part (c): trusted people / helpline
Part (d): justified choice

questions.q: A magazine says, "Hormones are released at random times, which is why two friends of the same age change at different times." Show that this explanation cannot match the chapter.
questions.a: The chapter says hormones are released at an appropriate time and in response to signals from the brain, so the release is not random. Hormones are produced in different parts of the body but are controlled by the brain's signals.
s: Released at an appropriate time
In response to signals from the brain
So 'random' contradicts the chapter

questions.q: A town's survey of 250 students aged 10-19 found that 40 had been offered a harmful substance by peers; 25 of them said NO, and 15 tried it. (a) Work out the percentage offered, the percentage of those offered who refused and the percentage who tried. (b) Why is it a concern that 15 tried? (c) What is the first step for those 15, and which national helpline can be used? (d) Why does the Abhiyaan focus on early-age children?
questions.a: (a) 40/250 = 16% were offered; 25/40 = 62.5% refused; 15/40 = 37.5% tried. (b) The substances are addictive, so a strong urge to take them again and again can develop and lead to regular use called substance abuse. (c) Seek help and support from family and friends and talk to trusted people such as parents or teachers; counselling and medical advice help; helpline 14446. (d) Its special focus is prevention among early-age children, before curiosity and excitement lead them to try.
s: Part (b): addictive, urge to repeat, substance abuse
Part (c): first step is seeking help from trusted people
Part (c): helpline 14446
Part (d): prevention among early-age children

questions.q: Pooja says, "So my mood swings are just hormones and I can do nothing about them." Evaluate her statement using this chapter and the earlier ones. Give four points and a verdict.
questions.a: Partly right. (1) Some hormones influence mood and behaviour, so she is right that hormones play a part. (2) The chapter says only some hormones do, and they are one reason among many changes. (3) Understanding how emotions influence behaviour helps in making better choices and responding thoughtfully. (4) Activities such as music, dance or sports, creative pursuits and social work support positive growth, and guidance from elders helps. Verdict: partly right, but 'nothing' is wrong.
s: Some hormones influence mood: right
Only some hormones, not all
Understanding emotions helps better choices
Positive activities and guidance of elders
Verdict: partly right, 'nothing' is wrong

questions.q:
Ritu, 13, notes in a school health journal: January, first period. February, taller by 3 cm in two months. March, sudden mood swings. Her friend Tara, also 13, has had mood swings but no period yet. Ritu's father says, "All of this is only because she has not eaten enough greens." Her aunt says, "The period is due to body chemicals, but mood is entirely her own choice."
(a) Name the chemicals the chapter credits with menstruation and some mood changes.
(b) What does the chapter say about when they are released, and what does it suggest about Tara?
(c) Which part of the aunt's statement agrees with the chapter, and which part does not?
(d) Whose statement is closer to the chapter, the father's or the aunt's? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Hormones. (b) They are produced in different parts of the body and released at an appropriate time in response to signals from the brain, so Tara's body is following its own timing and need not be at fault. (c) Agrees: the period is due to hormones. Does not: some hormones influence mood and behaviour, so mood is not entirely a matter of choice. (d) The aunt's, since the chapter attributes menstruation and other puberty signs mainly to hormones; the father's explanation rests on diet alone, although a nutritious diet is important for growth.
s: Part (a): hormones
Part (b): appropriate time on signals from brain; Tara need not be at fault
Part (c): agrees on period; mood influenced by some hormones
Part (d): aunt's is closer, with reason
